newsitem.title: UK: North Sea market quiet as buyers hold back.
newsitem.headline: North Sea market quiet as buyers hold back.

text.p: The North Sea physical market was quiet as buyers deterred by upwardly mobile futures prices held back from any further buying in a tight market with most second decade cargoes already placed, traders said.
Nov Brent futures rose to a high of $24.25 a barrel on Monday before easing back to $24.10 late in the afternoon. Nov/Dec was firmer at +52 cents after an earlier deal at +51.
The paper market was also subdued in the face of a fast-moving screen with much interest seen in the expanding Brent/Dubai spread.
Dec Brent/Dubai traded at +$2.32 and $2.35 as Dubai failed to keep up with Brent.

A London trader said that while the wide spread was deterring the sale of crudes priced against Brent into the Far East, refiners in South America and South Africa were beginning to show interest in Dubai.
"There is definitely one South American refiner sniffing around for Dubai, which is normal when prices fall to such levels," the trader said.
In the North Sea, two Brent cargoes loading in the Oct 20-23 window, both at Nov +10 cents, were the only wet deals heard.

"There's not much that has to be shifted. There are only end-month barrels and most of the buyers are covered in the 20-28 period, apart from Brent which is moving quite nicely," a North Sea trader said.

He added that Brent, which has been lagging behind as demand picked up for gas oil grades like Oseberg, had recovered and was moving further into backwardation. Another broker expected the next Brent deal to be done a few cents higher than Nov +10.
The only Brent cargo through the paper chains on Wednesday was kept by an equity holder.
